statement: Ten people sit evenly spaced around a round table. Each person shakes hands once with every other person except the two people sitting directly next to them. How many handshakes take place?

choices.misconception: I counted 7 handshakes for each of the 10 people and forgot that every handshake involves two people, so each was counted twice.
I counted every pair of the 10 people and forgot to leave out the pairs of neighbours.
I left out only one neighbour per person, giving 8 handshakes each, and then halved 10 x 8.
I took all 45 pairs and subtracted 20 neighbour pairs, counting each neighbouring pair once from each side.

hints: Count from one person's point of view first.
Overcount, then correct: count the handshakes each person makes and multiply by the number of people, then fix the fact that each handshake was seen from both ends.
Each person shakes 10 - 1 - 2 = 7 hands, so 10 x 7 = 70 counts every handshake twice.

solutions.reliable: Each person skips themselves and their two neighbours, so shakes 7 hands. Ten people times 7 is 70, but each handshake has been counted once by each of the two people in it, so there are 70 / 2 = 35. The transferable idea: count from each person, then divide by the number of times each object was counted.
solutions.elegant: There are 45 pairs of people in total, and exactly 10 of them are neighbours around the table, one pair per gap. 45 - 10 = 35.

whyOnTest: Handshake problems test whether you notice that counting from each person counts every handshake twice.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
